dialogue.content: 今日はよろしくお願いします。準備できましたら、始めますね
dialogue.English: Thank you for coming today. We'll begin whenever you're ready.

dialogue.content: はい。こちらこそ、宜しくお願い致します(_ _)
dialogue.English: Yes. Likewise, thank you for having me.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。相談員です。
dialogue.English: Hello. I'm the counselor.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。
dialogue.English: Hello.

dialogue.content: 返信ありがとうございます。はじめに、年代と性別を教えてください。
dialogue.English: Thank you for your reply. To begin, could you please tell me your age group and gender?

dialogue.content: はい。30代の女です。宜しくお願い致します(_ _)
dialogue.English: Yes. I'm a woman in my 30s. Thank you.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。今日は、どのようなご相談でしょうか？
dialogue.English: Thank you. What would you like to discuss today?

dialogue.content: パートへ行くのが苦痛だなぁと思っています…
dialogue.English: I'm finding it distressing to go to my part-time job...

dialogue.content: 苦痛だなと感じていらっしゃるのですね。
dialogue.English: So you're feeling that it's distressing.

dialogue.content: はい。起きて、あぁ、今日はパートだなと思うととても憂鬱です。
dialogue.English: Yes. When I wake up and think, 'Ah, I have my part-time job today,' I feel very depressed.

dialogue.content: 朝から憂鬱になってしまいますよね。もう少し詳しく教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: It must be depressing right from the morning. Could you tell me a little more about it?

dialogue.content: 人間関係、、かな。それで悩んでいる気がします。
dialogue.English: Probably the relationships... I think that's what's troubling me.

dialogue.content: パート先の人間関係で悩んでいらっしゃるのですね。それは、もやもやしますよね
dialogue.English: You're troubled by the relationships at your part-time job. That must feel frustrating.

dialogue.content: ですね。行かなくていいならホント行きたくないです。周りとうまく馴染めなくて…
dialogue.English: Right. If I didn't have to go, I really wouldn't. I just can't seem to fit in with the others...

dialogue.content: 周りとうまく馴染めないとお感じなのですね。
dialogue.English: You feel that you’re not able to fit in with those around you.

dialogue.content: はい。特にリーダーからは、全く好かれていないと思います。
dialogue.English: Yes. Especially the leader—I don't think they like me at all.

dialogue.content: それは、行きたくなくなりますよね
dialogue.English: That would make you not want to go, wouldn't it?

dialogue.content: 行きたくないです。
dialogue.English: I don't want to go.

dialogue.content: ええ。リーダーから好かれていないとは、どのようなときに感じますか？
dialogue.English: I understand. In what situations do you feel that the leader doesn’t like you?

dialogue.content: 私には話しかけてくれません。必要なことがある時は普通に話してはくれるのですが…
dialogue.English: They don't initiate conversation with me. They'll talk to me normally if it's necessary for work, but...

dialogue.content: みんなとは楽しそうに談笑してるんですけどね…
dialogue.English: But they seem to chat and laugh happily with everyone else...

dialogue.content: それは、少しショックですよね。
dialogue.English: That must be a bit of a shock.

dialogue.content: 仲間外れにされているように感じてしまいますよね。
dialogue.English: It must make you feel like you're being left out.

dialogue.content: はい…ショックですね。なんで私だけ話してもらえないのかな…って。
dialogue.English: Yes... it is a shock. I keep thinking, 'Why am I the only one they won't talk to...?'

dialogue.content: 私も明るいほうじゃないのですが、極力笑顔で頑張っているつもりなんです…
dialogue.English: I'm not the most cheerful person, but I try my best to smile as much as possible...

dialogue.content: 笑顔でがんばっていらっしゃるのですね。でも、気持ちは沈んでしまいそうですよね。いつごろから、リーダーのそのような態度が続いているのですか？
dialogue.English: You’ve been trying your best to smile. Even so, it must bring your mood down. How long has the leader been treating you this way?

dialogue.content: はい。笑顔で頑張ってもそれが報われないから、気分はどんどん沈んで…行きたくないなって思うようになってきましたね。リーダーとは割と最初からそんな感じなので、約2年間そんな関係です。
dialogue.English: Yes. Even if I try to smile, it's not reciprocated, so my mood just keeps sinking... and I've started to feel like I don't want to go. It's been like that with the leader more or less from the beginning, so our relationship has been this way for about two years.

dialogue.content: 2年間も…それは、とても長く、しんどいですよね。
dialogue.English: For two years... that's a very long time, and it's really tough.

dialogue.content: 頑張って働いていらっしゃいましたね。
dialogue.English: You've been working so hard.

dialogue.content: リーダーとは最初から、そのような関係だということですが、きっかけみたいなものはありますか？何か思い当たることなど
dialogue.English: You said it's been like that with the leader from the start, but was there any kind of trigger? Does anything come to mind?

dialogue.content: はい。しんどいです…有難うございます…。笑顔でいてもダメ、頑張って仕事してもダメ、私自身が受け入れてもらえない気がして辛いです。
dialogue.English: Yes, it's tough... Thank you... It doesn't matter if I smile, it doesn't matter if I work hard; I feel like I'm just not being accepted, and it's painful.

dialogue.content: どうなんでしょう。うーん、ちょっと待ってくださいね。
dialogue.English: I wonder. Hmm, let me think for a moment.

dialogue.content: はい。おまちしますね
dialogue.English: Of course. Take your time.

dialogue.content: 何をしても「ダメ」と決めつけられて、受け入れられていないとお感じなのですね
dialogue.English: So you feel that no matter what you do, you're judged as "not good enough" and aren't being accepted.

dialogue.content: リーダーに好かれている人は、明るく元気な人が多い印象です。ガハハ！みたいな。何か失敗しても、すいませーん！って明るく言える人。私は明るくないので、ダメなのかなぁ…
dialogue.English: The people the leader likes tend to be cheerful and energetic. The type who laughs out loud. The kind of person who can make a mistake and say "Oops, sorry!" in a bright way. I'm not that cheerful, so maybe that's why I'm no good...

dialogue.content: 私が近くにいても無視なのに、そのすぐ私の隣にいる人には、「どう？できそう？」って話しかけてて…
dialogue.English: Even when I'm right there, they ignore me, but then they'll turn to the person right next to me and ask, "How's it going? Think you can manage?"...

dialogue.content: 私のことは心配してくれないのかな…どうして私のことは無視するのかな…って、悲しくて…
dialogue.English: I wonder if they don't care about me... or why they ignore me... It just makes me sad...

dialogue.content: なるほど…リーダには明るく元気な人が好かれている。あなたが、近くにいても無視されるのは、とてもつらいし、悲しくなりますよね
dialogue.English: I see... so the leader prefers cheerful and energetic people. Being ignored even when you're right there must be very painful and sad for you.

dialogue.content: このような状況を他の誰かに相談されたことはありますか？
dialogue.English: Have you talked to anyone else about this situation?

dialogue.content: はい。悲しい、辛い、そんな思いです。
dialogue.English: Yes. It's sad, it's painful... that's how I feel.

dialogue.content: 同じ部署で働く子に冗談っぽく話したことはありますね。（その子はリーダーに好かれてるんですけどね…。）そしたら、
dialogue.English: I've mentioned it jokingly to a coworker in the same department. (She's one of the ones the leader likes, though...) And then she said,

dialogue.content: （ええ。聞いていますね）
dialogue.English: (Yes, I'm listening.)

dialogue.content: 「リーダーは気分に波があるからね〜。ちょっと難しいよね」とは言ってました。でも、好かれてて羨ましいなぁと思ってしまいます。
dialogue.English: She said, "The leader can be moody, you know. They're a bit difficult." But I can't help but feel envious that she's liked.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。うらやましいとお感じなのですね。2年間働いてきて、今のパート先の仕事内容は、どのように感じていますか？
dialogue.English: I see. So you feel envious. Having worked there for two years, how do you feel about the work itself at your current job?

dialogue.content: 羨ましいですね。みんなで楽しく話してて。仕事内容は、苦じゃないんですよね。みんなママさんなので、子供が熱出したので休みます！も全然アリな部署で。待遇よし、仕事内容よし、勤務時間よし、なので、ホントあとはリーダーだけの問題です…
dialogue.English: I am envious—seeing everyone chatting happily together. The work itself isn't a problem for me. Everyone's a mom, so it's a department where saying, 'My child has a fever, so I'll be taking the day off!' is totally acceptable. The benefits are good, the work is good, the hours are good—so honestly, the only problem is the leader...

dialogue.content: なるほど…待遇や、仕事内容などは良いと感じていらっしゃるから、2年間続けていらっしゃったのですね。だからこそ、リーダーとの人間関係さえと思ってしまいますね
dialogue.English: I see... so you've continued for two years because you feel the benefits and the work itself are good. That must make you think, if only it weren't for the relationship with the leader.

dialogue.content: はい。やはり子供は突然体調崩すので、当日自分が休む分のシフトを埋めたりしなくて休めるのは本当に助かるんです。なので、リーダーとのことは考えないようにして働いてきました。
dialogue.English: Yes. Kids get sick suddenly, so being able to take the day off without having to find coverage for my shift is a huge help. That's why I've tried to work without thinking about the issue with the leader.

dialogue.content: でも、仲良くなる必要もないのかな…とか、仕事ができてればいいかな…とも思うんです。
dialogue.English: But then I also think, maybe I don't need to be friends with them... or maybe it's enough just to do my job well...

dialogue.content: ええ。とても良い職場なのですね。今まで、お話を聞いて思ったのですが、
dialogue.English: Yes. It sounds like a very good workplace in many ways. From what you've shared so far,

dialogue.content: リーダーの顔色をうかがってお仕事をするのは、とてもつらいし、居心地が悪くなりますよね
dialogue.English: Having to work while constantly worrying about the leader's mood must be very draining and uncomfortable.

dialogue.content: あなたが、おっしゃる通り、仕事をしっかりとしていれば、必ずしも仲良くなる必要がないと思いましたが、いかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: As you said, I was thinking that as long as you do your job properly, you don't necessarily have to be friends. What are your thoughts on that?

dialogue.content: そうですよね。仲良くお喋りするために仕事へ行っているわけではないですもんね。お金を稼ぎに行くわけで。
dialogue.English: That's true. I'm not going to work to chat and be friendly, after all. I'm going there to earn money.

dialogue.content: でもなんていうか、寂しいし悲しくなっちゃうんですよね。。
dialogue.English: But, how do I put it... I still end up feeling lonely and sad.

dialogue.content: ええ。パート先へいっている時間は、さみしい、悲しいと思ってしまうのですよね。
dialogue.English: Yes. During the time you're at your part-time job, you end up feeling lonely and sad.

dialogue.content: そうですね。５時間だけなんですけど、一気に疲れるというか。
dialogue.English: That's right. It's only for five hours, but it's incredibly draining.

dialogue.content: ええ。リーダーに気を使っていると、一気に疲れてしまいますよね。リーダーよりも、上の上司または、人事のような機関はありますか？
dialogue.English: Yes. Being so mindful of the leader must be exhausting. Is there a superior above the leader, or a department like HR?

dialogue.content: 人事はないのですが、リーダーの上はもう一番偉い人になってしまいますね。上の人とはきちんとお話したこともないんです。このこと、誰にもお話ししたくないんです…
dialogue.English: There's no HR, and the person above the leader is the head of the company. I've never really spoken properly with them. And I don't want to talk about this with anyone...

dialogue.content: 自分がすごく惨めに思えるから…
dialogue.English: Because it makes me feel so pathetic...

dialogue.content: 挨拶をきちんとしてもダメで、笑顔でもダメで、極力明るくお話ししてもダメ。あとは何があるんだろう
dialogue.English: Greeting them properly doesn't work, smiling doesn't work, trying my best to be cheerful doesn't work. What else is there for me to do?

dialogue.content: そのような状況だったのですね。誰にもお話できないと感じたから、こちらにきていただいたのですね。
dialogue.English: So that's the situation. You felt you couldn't talk to anyone about it, which is why you came here.

dialogue.content: そうですね。私を知ってる人には話せなくて…（知られたくなくて…）
dialogue.English: That's right. I can't talk about it with people who know me... (I don't want them to know...)

dialogue.content: ええ。何をしても「ダメ」という否定をされた気持ちになってしまうのですね
dialogue.English: I understand. You feel that no matter what you do, you're being rejected and told you're "not good enough".

dialogue.content: そうなんですよね。私自身を強く否定されている感じがあって、、
dialogue.English: Exactly. I feel like my very self is being strongly rejected.

dialogue.content: 否定されていると、そこから逃げ出したくなりますよね
dialogue.English: When you feel rejected, it makes you want to run away.

dialogue.content: はい。つまらないダメな人間だなと思うと、もう仕事に行きたくなくて。転職サイト見たりしちゃいますね〜
dialogue.English: Yes. When I think I'm such a boring, useless person, I just don't want to go to work anymore. I even find myself looking at job search websites.

dialogue.content: 今のこのような状況を他の人に知られたくないのは、どうしてだと感じていますか？
dialogue.English: Why do you feel you don't want others to know about your current situation?

dialogue.content: そんなことで悩んでるの？って言われる気がしますね。前に唯一話をした子には、真面目に考えすぎだよ！と言われました。
dialogue.English: I feel like they'd say, "You're worried about *that*?" The one person I did talk to before told me, "You're taking it too seriously!"

dialogue.content: 「そんなこと」とは、言われるとそれ以上何も言えなくなってしまいますね
dialogue.English: Being told "something like that" can really shut you down from saying anything more.

dialogue.content: 今までお聞きしたことをまとめさせていただくと、
dialogue.English: Let me summarize what I've heard so far.

dialogue.content: パート先のリーダーから、好かれていないと感じていて、何をしても「ダメ」と否定され、職場に行くのが苦痛だと感じていらっしゃるということですね。
dialogue.English: You feel that you're disliked by the leader at your part-time job, that no matter what you do you're rejected as "not good enough," and that you find it distressing to go to work. Is that correct?

dialogue.content: はい（泣）その通りです
dialogue.English: Yes... (crying) that's exactly right.

dialogue.content: 人事などはなく、周りの人にも相談しにくい状況なのですね
dialogue.English: And there's no HR, and it's a difficult situation to discuss with those around you.

dialogue.content: そうですね。きちんと話したいと思える人は周りにいないですし、話したいとも思っていない…気もします。（話すと虚しくなる気がして）
dialogue.English: That's right. There's no one around me I feel I can really talk to, and I don't think I even want to... (I feel like talking about it will just make me feel empty.)

dialogue.content: ええ。話したいと思える人がいないということなのですね。提案なのですが、辛く、悲しいと感じている職場で、このまま働き続けるか
dialogue.English: I see. So there's no one you feel you can talk to. I'd like to make a suggestion. You could either continue working at this job where you feel pained and sad,

dialogue.content: 違う環境を求めて職場を変えるか
dialogue.English: or you could seek a different environment and change jobs.

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: どちらのほうに考えがありますか？
dialogue.English: Which way are you leaning?

dialogue.content: うーん、、、、、待遇優先なので、まだホントの限界を感じるまでは、今の職場で頑張る気持ちのほうが強いかもしれません。
dialogue.English: Hmm... the benefits are my priority, so until I really feel I've reached my limit, I think I'm more inclined to try and stick it out at my current job.

dialogue.content: ええ。待遇が大事だとお感じなのですね。
dialogue.English: I see. So you feel the benefits are important.

dialogue.content: そうですね、やっぱり当日休めるっていうのはママ的にはすごく助かります。
dialogue.English: Yes, being able to take a day off on short notice is a huge help as a mom.

dialogue.content: ただ、ココロの限界を迎えるまでというのは、とてもあなたが心配です。
dialogue.English: However, waiting until you reach your mental breaking point... that makes me very worried for you.

dialogue.content: 有難うございます。そんな風に言っていただいて*ᴗ ᴗ)⁾⁾
dialogue.English: Thank you. I appreciate you saying that.

dialogue.content: とても今までがんばっていらっしゃって、
dialogue.English: You've been trying so hard up to this point,

dialogue.content: 家庭にまで持ち込みたくなくて、家でも悩みを話せなくて悩んでいました。
dialogue.English: I didn't want to bring it home with me, so I was also struggling with the fact that I couldn't talk about my worries at home.

dialogue.content: 工夫されながら、働いてこられたあなたは、すごいと思います。家でも話せずにいたのですね
dialogue.English: I think it's amazing that you've been managing and working through all of this. And you haven't been able to talk about it at home, either.

dialogue.content: 有難うございます(_ _)はい。旦那に言ったらきっと、「辞めたらいい」と、すぐに結論を出されるので…
dialogue.English: Thank you. Yes. If I told my husband, I'm sure he'd immediately jump to the conclusion and say, "Then you should just quit."

dialogue.content: なるほど、夫さんにはすぐに答えを出されてしまう
dialogue.English: I see—your husband tends to give you an immediate answer.

dialogue.content: そうなんです。過程はほぼ無視で結論を出されるので、こちらが置いてきぼりを喰らうんです…
dialogue.English: Exactly. He pretty much ignores the process and just gives a conclusion, which leaves me feeling left behind...

dialogue.content: 辞めたいけど辞められないから悩んでるんだけどなー…って。
dialogue.English: It's like, 'The reason I'm struggling is because I want to quit but I can't...'

dialogue.content: ええ。共感してほしいですよね。
dialogue.English: Yes. You want him to empathize with you, don't you?

dialogue.content: ホントですよ。まずは私の話や気持ちを聞いてほしい。
dialogue.English: I really do. I just want him to listen to what I have to say and how I feel first.

dialogue.content: 「聞いて」と相手に伝えてみるというのも良いかもしれませんね
dialogue.English: It might be a good idea to try telling him, "I just want you to listen."

dialogue.content: そうですよね、もう諦めちゃってるので話をすることもしなくなりましたが、一度また向き合うのも大事かもしれません。辞める、と言う前に旦那の考えを聞きたいですし。
dialogue.English: You're right. I've sort of given up, so I stopped talking to him about it, but maybe it's important to try and face it again. I'd like to hear his thoughts before I say I'm quitting.

dialogue.content: 向き合ってみるのは、大事なことかもしれません。
dialogue.English: Trying to face it again may be an important step.

dialogue.content: はい。話す努力をしてみようと思いますっ。
dialogue.English: Yes. I'll try to make an effort to talk to him.

dialogue.content: 人に話すことは、みじめに思うとおっしゃっていましたが、今まで、とても頑張って働いていらっしゃったことは胸を張っていいと思いますし、
dialogue.English: You mentioned that talking to people about this makes you feel pathetic, but I think you should be proud of how hard you've worked all this time,

dialogue.content: 堂々とされていいと思います
dialogue.English: and you deserve to carry yourself with confidence.

dialogue.content: 有難うございます…T^T
dialogue.English: Thank you... T^T

dialogue.content: お時間が過ぎてしまって申し訳ございません。
dialogue.English: I'm sorry, we've gone over our time.

dialogue.content: あ！こちらこそすみません💦
dialogue.English: Oh! No, I'm sorry as well.

dialogue.content: 気づかず💦
dialogue.English: I didn't realize.

dialogue.content: （いえいえ、私は大丈夫です）
dialogue.English: (No, no, it's fine with me.)

dialogue.content: リーダーの方と、良い距離を保ちつつ、無理をなさらずお仕事なさってくださいね
dialogue.English: Please try to keep a healthy distance from your leader, and don't push yourself too hard at work.

dialogue.content: はい！有難うございます(_ _)頑張れる力がまだ残っていることに気づかせてもらえました。
dialogue.English: Yes! Thank you. You've helped me realize that I still have some strength left to keep going.

dialogue.content: もう限界かも、、と思っていたけど、それでも待遇の良さは諦められないので、もう少しだけ頑張っていこうと思います。
dialogue.English: I was thinking I might be at my limit, but I can't give up the good benefits, so I'm going to try to hang in there a little longer.

dialogue.content: ええ。コロナ禍ですし、お体にくれぐれも気を付けながら、お過ごしくださいね
dialogue.English: Yes. And with the pandemic, please be sure to take very good care of yourself.

dialogue.content: はいっ。有難うございます！先生もお体ご自愛ください。
dialogue.English: Yes! Thank you! Please take care of yourself as well.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました。以上で相談を終了させていただきますね。
dialogue.English: Thank you very much. This concludes our session.

dialogue.content: はい^ ^
dialogue.English: Okay. ^^

dialogue.content: （ほんと長くなってすみません
dialogue.English: (I'm really sorry this ran long.)

dialogue.content: （こちらこそです💦」
dialogue.English: (No, it was me! 💦)

dialogue.content: ロールプレイ終了しますね。
dialogue.English: We'll end the role-play now.

dialogue.content: （長々喋ってしまいましたー！💦）
dialogue.English: (I ended up talking for so long! 💦)

dialogue.content: はい^ ^有難うございました！
dialogue.English: Okay. ^^ Thank you very much!
